## New cross-domain connections
- **[2026-11-12] Lightfin's adaptation page has three tracks. The two that would reach an audience, book and video, have been "Exploring" since April because each waits on a publishing or production decision. The N.D. Austin episode Fred finished this week describes a fourth format that needs neither: stage one case as a one-off live mystery for a few children.** [[lightfin/adaptation-overview]] lists book, video and story expansion, with games as "future". [[lightfin/story-bible]] says audience participation is "core to the format, not incidental", yet the only participation the show has is the 15-second pause before the reveal. [[podcasts/podcast-death-sex-and-money-real-life-willy-wonka-tony-hawk]] gives a working method in three parts. Open with unexplained objects: Hawk's staff found a shovel, a locked briefcase and keys on their desks. Build from what the players already share: the funeral board game was assembled from mechanics the friends had played for years. End it for good: that game was played once and buried. [[lightfin/ep-000-treasure-of-the-esperanza]] already supplies all three. It has planted gold coins in a desk drawer, two suspects to question (Sidney Stonefish and Blue Marlin), and a treasure to dig up at the end. The podcast page's own note links Austin to game design in general and to the Yousef episode; it does not mention Lightfin. A live case would also test something the book track assumes and has never checked: that 5–8s only "guess along" while 9–13s can follow a clue trail, which is the whole basis for the picture-book and chapter-book split. It is also a paper prototype for the game track in [[games/overview]]. **Smallest next step:** add "Track 4: live case (one-off)" to the adaptation page's options and write Case 0 as three clue stations plus the planted-coin reveal. Run it once with children from both age bands and note which clues each band solved without help.

- **[2026-11-12] Finance's stablecoin page argues that Washington is building a captive buyer of Treasury bills out of stablecoin demand. It treats that demand as one number. This week's first podcast pick, Scam Inc, is about one part of it: scam compounds that move stolen money over crypto rails.** [[finance/investor-letters/source-bond-market-bessent-stablecoins-2026-09-02]] puts Tether at about $183.6bn of a $308bn market, with about $140.6bn in Treasury-linked reserves, and quotes Bessent's projection of 10x growth by 2030. It never asks who holds the tokens. [[podcasts/suggestions]] (week of 2026-11-12) describes Scam Inc as an eight-part Economist series on the pig-butchering economy in Southeast Asia, "including how stolen money is laundered through crypto rails". From outside the wiki, and to be checked against the series: UNODC reporting has named USDT, mostly on Tron, as the preferred rail for those networks. If that holds, the largest holder in the Treasury-buyer thesis is also the issuer most exposed to enforcement, and the 10x path depends on demand that the same government wants to grow and to police. Neither side is in the wiki. [[crypto/crypto-overview]] tracks only delta-neutral designs (USDN, USDe), and [[crypto/defi-watchlist]] links the Bessent page for reserve exposure only. This is a different gap from the 10-22 entry, which was about exploit risk in Fred's own tokens. **If Fred listens:** note which token and chain the series names and any estimate of the sums involved, and add them to the Bessent page as a caveat on the quality of the demand.

None today. The Carlisle, Magic Formula and Kelly angles from Books and Podcasts were already logged in October.

## New investigation idea
- **[2026-11-11] Health has not changed since 08-03, and its "Biomarkers Being Tracked" table is still empty. The only new health material in three months, the Sahar Yousef attention episode Fred finished on 10-31, is filed under Podcasts only. It includes a cheap test whose result Fred's phone already records.** [[health/overview]] lists two sources and [[health/my-protocol]] has had "[to be added]" in every table since 05-01. Earlier ideas here asked for lab tests (homocysteine, Omega-3 Index) and supplements (creatine, 07-05), which need a purchase or a clinic visit, and none has happened. [[podcasts/podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-phone-addiction-scientist-dr-sahar-yousef]] reports that switching the phone to grayscale cut use by about 1 hour a day in her Berkeley lab, and puts context-switching at about 47 seconds per screen and about 2 hours a day lost. Daily screen time and pickups are logged automatically by the phone (Screen Time / Digital Wellbeing), so this is the one marker that needs no lab, no purchase and no new habit to measure. Learning already holds the companion practice: [[learning/source-ferriss-deloading]]'s "screen-free Saturdays", a page this file had never cited. **Concrete step:** note this week's daily screen-time average and pickups as the baseline, run grayscale for 14 days, and enter before/after as the first row of my-protocol's biomarker table (target: about −60 min/day, Yousef's figure). File the Yousef page under [[health/overview]]'s Sources at the same time, so Health gets its first source since August.

## New cross-domain connection
- **[2026-11-11] The 11-06 entry proposed borrowing the Terrain Autobattler's savings rule for the Children's Financial Literacy Game. The same economy also has the opposite button: reroll, which costs 2 gold for a fresh random set of offers. That is the variable-reward "slot machine" mechanic the Yousef episode Fred just finished warns about. In an autobattler the choice between saving for interest and paying to reroll is the core decision, so this is the save-or-gamble lesson a kids' money game is trying to teach.** [[games/terrain-autobattler-factions-units-economy]] sets the reroll at 2 gold and interest at +1 per 10 held (max +3). It also publishes shop odds by level (level 1–2: 100% 1-cost; 4-costs first at level 5, 2%), and its AI opponents carry a "reroll threshold". [[podcasts/podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-phone-addiction-scientist-dr-sahar-yousef]] describes variable rewards as working like a slot machine and says infinite feeds work by removing stopping points. The autobattler already has the two defences she names. The odds are posted, and the 35-second planning timer ([[games/project-terrain-autobattler]]) is a hard stopping point on rerolling. A kids' version that copies only the savings half would lose the lesson. A copy that keeps rerolls but drops the timer and the posted odds would teach the habit she warns about. **Design rule for `raw/games/Childrens Financial Literacy Game.md`:** keep the reroll, keep both defences, and show the price of each reroll next to the interest it gives up (2 gold spent at 20 held moves the player to 18 and costs the +1 interest on the next round). The 2,000-fight harness extended to full matches (see 11-06) could then measure the reroll threshold at which `aggressive` stops beating `greedy`. That number would be the game's answer to "when is gambling worth it?"
